messages.subject: plotting data with missing values?
parts:
Hi,

when using ezMixed() to analyze data with missing values (some missing subjects) I find something like this:

> myAOV = ezMixed(data=myData,dv=.(gain),random=.(subject,condId),fixed=.(c, b, a))
> print(myAOV$summary)


            effect error warning      bits
1                 a FALSE   FALSE -2.524781
2                 b FALSE   FALSE -2.656061
3                 c FALSE   FALSE -2.725315
4              a:b FALSE   FALSE 20.780244
5              a:c FALSE   FALSE -2.836513
6              b:c FALSE   FALSE -2.271222
7           a:b:c FALSE   FALSE  8.312715

I understand that this analysis shows that there's evidence suggesting  an effect of a:b and the intercept a:b:c
How should I proceed to plot the results of this analysis using ezPlot()? or could you recommend a different tool for that?
Thanks for your help, it's greatly appreciated.

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] plotting data with missing values?
parts:
First, apologies for letting your message sit in the moderation queue
for so long; I must have inadvertently skipped the notification email.

You want to use ezPredict() to generate a predictions object from the
model then use ezPlot2() to visualize the predictions object. for
example:

myFit = myAOV$models$"a:b:c"$unrestricted
myPreds = ezPredict(
myFit
, effect_variability_only = TRUE
)
myPlot = ezPlot2(
predictions = myPreds
, x = .(a)
, split = .(b)
, col = .(c)
)
print(myPlot$plot)

Note that the error bars are 95% CIs. Slightly more useful CIs can be
achieved if your variables are coded with contrasts that dissociate
the intercept variance from the effect variances, in which case you
can change "effect_variability_only = TRUE" above to
"effect_variability_only = FALSE" (or just omit the argument
altogether as FALSE is its default), yielding 95%CIs that omit the
intercept variance, therefore permitting comparison of points on the
raw scale that should (generally) mesh with the comparisons you'd get
by collapsing the predictions to difference scores and difference
score CIs. If your variables have only two levels, you can also
explicitly compute difference scores via the "diff" argument to
ezPlot2, for example:

myPlot2 = ezPlot2(
predictions = myPreds
, x = .(a)
, diff = .(b,c) #double difference score of two 2-level variables
)
print(my_Plot2$plot)
